lines.text: It’s project time! Design and build a text adventure with at least three rooms, an inventory, a locked door, a treasure to win and a torch that runs out.
A text adventure is a story where the player types commands like north or take.
A variable called room remembers where they are. if and elif decide what each command does in each room.
Start with an empty list: inventory = [].
When the player picks something up, use inventory.append("key").
Later, if "key" in inventory: can unlock a door.
A while loop keeps the game running while playing is True.
Finding the treasure wins.
Running out of moves loses.
def show_status(): gives a name to a chunk of code.
Call it with show_status() whenever you need it.
Functions keep long programs tidy, and Level 2 goes much deeper.
The word def makes a new command called describe_room.
We write it once, then call it twice with different room names.
The bag starts empty, then we append a key.
Because key is in the inventory, the locked door opens.
The while loop keeps asking for commands while playing is True.
Each elif checks the room AND the command, so north only works from the hall.
Real game designers sketch a map before they write any code.
Build one room at a time and test it, so bugs stay small and easy to find.
Great work! Let’s remember what we learned.
Now plan it, build it, test it, and share it!
